title: Jonas tends the greenhouse
topic: A gardener named Jonas tends a greenhouse in spring: dry soil, a hose, bees, compost, the first blossoms
tail_E: Before he leaves, Jonas gives the thirsty plants a drink of
target_note: 'water' is predictable from the context (dry soil after a warm week, a hose between the beds, a gardener about to leave) and the tail 'gives the thirsty plants a drink of'; the word 'water' (also 'waters', 'watering') and its German equivalents (Wasser, gießen) occur nowhere in the units or in the tail. ' water' is a single Pythia token (id 1824); Pythia-160m ranks it first after the all-English context (p ~ 0.46), after the all-German context (p ~ 0.34) and after the tail alone (p ~ 0.62): in this family the target is carried mainly by the tail ('a drink of'), so the context effect is expected to be smaller than in F02/F03.
author: LS-NEQ stimulus authoring (F04A, gardener Jonas)
notes: Formulation A. Ten meaning units: Jonas tends a greenhouse / the sun warms the roof / Jonas plants cucumbers / the soil is dry / a hose lies between the beds / bees fly in / the neighbour brings compost / Jonas removes yellow leaves / the first blossoms open / Jonas locks the greenhouse. The words 'water', 'Wasser' and 'gießen' are deliberately absent so that 'water' can serve as the target. German predicates avoid separable verbs ('einfangen', 'abschließen' avoided: 'verschließt' in unit 10). Unit 9 uses the reflexive 'sich öffnen' (reflexive pronoun inside pred). Subjects alternate between Jonas, objects and natural agents (sun, soil, hose, bees, blossoms) and another person (neighbour). Unit 9 reads naturally in German; units 1 and 10 read naturally in English.
